commit.message:
fix(advisor-orchestrator-worker): round-3 field fixes from a live self-run

The skill ran the full loop on its own source and produced a patch spec
for itself: worker W1 reproduced the exact brief-in-argument injection
bug, got redispatched, and the mandatory advisor pass caught mechanical
gaps round 2 missed. Adopting the substantive findings:

- Empty-key guard: dispatch fails fast if neither GEMINI_API_KEY nor
  GOOGLE_API_KEY is set, instead of silently calling with an empty key
- Per-worker subshell: each backgrounded worker runs in its own subshell
  so parallel cd/cleanup and traps can't collide
- Timeouts: worker curl (--max-time) and advisor call (timeout 300) so a
  hung call can't stall the whole wave
- Honest agy limitation: agy -p has no documented prompt-file/stdin
  input, so tool-worker prompts must stay short/sanitized/trusted rather
  than routing an arbitrary brief through the argument
- Degraded output labeled [DEGRADED: role]; empty-dir+minimal-env called
  what it is (reduces leakage, not a full sandbox)

Worker/advisor snippets moved to fenced blocks for clarity. All four
findings encoded as behavioral-eval expectations so they can't regress.
Lint strict, security scan (clean on the shell snippets), and trigger
routing all pass; body 135 lines.

fix(advisor-executor-worker): field feedback round 2 — injection-safe dispatch

From a real Codex run:

commit.message:
ci: adopt addyosmani/agent-skills' full tier model — no reinvented wheels

Tier 2 (trigger & routing) is now automated in CI instead of a manual
protocol: run_trigger_evals.py checks that positive prompts clear the
near-miss negatives on description vocabulary alone, and — once the
catalog has 2+ skills — that positives rank their own skill first and
no two descriptions near-collide. Reasoning-triggered cases (necromancer
mode) are marked lexical:false and covered by tier 3.

Tier 3 (behavioral) adopts skill-creator's evals.json schema verbatim,
so Anthropic's run_eval.py, benchmarking, and eval viewer work against
our files unmodified. project-graveyard's four behavioral cases written
in that schema.

The evals README tier table now uses Addy's names for Addy's tiers, and
marks the two tiers that are ours because our skills ship executable
code and his don't (security scan, deterministic script evals).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci: strict lint now fails text-only prompt dumps — the gate matches the bar

The audit found the hole: --strict only promoted the 500-line limit, so
a contributor could PR exactly the kind of text-only skill this repo
deleted 19 of, and every check would pass green. Now the no-prompt-dump
rule is a strict-mode error. Proven with a negative test: a synthetic
prompt-dump skill fails CI lint; project-graveyard still passes clean.

Also: provenance headers on both vendored tools pointing at their
origin, so the copies can't silently drift unnoticed.

commit.message:
feat: add project-graveyard agent skill

Scans your machine for dead side projects, autopsies why each one died
from its git history (deploy fear, payments wall, killed-by-newer-
project kill-chain, boilerplate death), shows your personal death
patterns, and resurrects the one with a pulse. The agent interviews
you on ambiguous deaths, world-checks what got easier since, executes
the resurrection plan, and tracks relapses on every resurrection it
prescribes.

Python stdlib, offline, read-only. The installable folder contains
only what runs at runtime; the 16-assertion executable eval lives in
awesome_agent_skills/evals/ — run it from the clone before installing.
One-command install via the skills CLI (70+ agents).

Also: self-improving-agent-skills drops its toy example files — its
examples endpoint now surfaces sibling skills from this repo, so the
app demos on real skills.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore: remove 19 basic prompt-dump skills

commit.message:
fix: remove stdlib modules from requirements.txt

asyncio and uuid are Python standard library modules (available since
Python 3.4+). Listing them in requirements.txt is unnecessary and can
install unrelated PyPI packages with the same name, causing conflicts.

Affected files (8 total):
- starter_ai_agents: openai_research_agent, mixture_of_agents,
  ai_meme_generator_agent_browseruse
- mcp_ai_agents: github_mcp_agent, browser_mcp_agent
- ai_agent_framework_crash_course: 5_1_in_memory_conversation_agent,
  5_2_persistent_conversation_agent
- advanced_ai_agents: ai_financial_coach_agent

fix: guard against empty choices and None message in DeepSeek API responses

Add safety checks before accessing deepseek_response.choices[0].message
to prevent IndexError and AttributeError when the API returns empty or
filtered responses.

Closes #817
